_comment: Native Word COMMENT capture. Word stores editor comments in
word/comments.xml, each carrying a w:author; the anchors (which span each comment
is attached to) live in word/document.xml as w:commentRangeStart/End by w:id. Only
comments whose author is on THIS Creative-Services whitelist are surfaced into the
HTML, anchored just BEFORE the element they comment on. The human gold strips ALL
comments, so — exactly like the CS notes — these are converter-only v1-workflow
surfaces, marked so that comparisons with the human build skip them (via the cv2-comment
class, and in text via the author-name prefix). Across the corpus, most comments
in the writers templates come from whitelisted authors, and no variant spelling
of the six names is missed.

render.form: Note from {author}: {text}
render.note: A captured reviewer comment renders 'Note from {author}: {text}', red AND BOLD, the author + text verbatim — never reworded, never author-dropped, never substituted with another prefix (Change Ledger CL-0010). legacy_form holds the bare '{author}: {text}' lead, used when env NOTESCHEME_OFF is set or Emit_Templates red_flag.ledger_note_scheme.enabled is false. The cv2-comment class marks these notes, and text comparisons skip paragraphs led by 'Note from' (or a legacy author-name prefix). Placed as a direct child of the body content region, immediately BEFORE the anchored element (not nested in its row/col/activity).

content_filter.omit_boilerplate: (used\s+(with|by|under)\b|with permission\b|used in online learning|public domain|creative commons|crown copyright|copyright act|all rights reserved|cc0\b|©|\bte kura (created|produced|made|owned)|links?\s+only\b|extract only|okay to use|\ball (istock|you ?tube|shutterstock)\b|licen[cs]e\.?\s*$|^link$|^links?\b)
content_filter.action_keep: (\bplease\b|\breplace\b|\brecreate\b|\bre-create\b|\bembed\b|\binsert\b|\bremove\b|\bcrop\b|\bresize\b|\bswap\b|\bdelete\b|\boverlay\b|\bjumble\b|\bsource\b|can you\b|can we\b|could you\b|could we\b|designer to\b|we (cannot|can'?t|are unable|need)\b|\?\s*$)
content_filter.note: OMIT non-actionable repetitive commentary the designer needn't action: a comment is dropped iff it matches omit_boilerplate (copyright / permission / 'used in online learning within the exception for education' / 'Te Kura created' / attribution / © / 'link only' …) AND matches NO action_keep signal — so a MIXED note ('Replace with iStock. Used with permission.') is KEPT. Applies to ALL six whitelisted authors uniformly. Most whitelisted comments are this copyright/ack boilerplate; the actionable designer instructions are what remain. Disable to surface every whitelisted comment regardless of content.

media_match.note: A whitelisted comment anchored to a MEDIA LIST table row (which the converter doesn't render as body content) is surfaced into the MAIN module content, BEFORE the body element that links the same media item. The match key is the row's hyperlink URL (DocxExtractor records it as comment.rowUrl): the same URL appears as an <a href> in the body where the writer referenced the image/video, so the comment inserts just before that element (or its interactive box), at body level — same placement rules as every other comment. Only KEPT (actionable) comments surface (the content_filter still omits the copyright/permission commentary); the comment's own anchor block (the media table) is excluded, and each surfaces once. Almost every commented media row carries a URL that also appears in the body. Env MEDIAMATCH_OFF turns this off (media-list comments stay unsurfaced).
media_match.id_match_note: The match key extends beyond the EXACT URL to the extracted MEDIA REFERENCE NUMBER: the iStock id (gm-form e.g. gm1382010801 OR the CDN /id/NNN form) and the YouTube video id. The body shows most images as a Mode-P placeholder (no live <a href>), but the writer's source URL — and therefore the iStock id — is recorded on the image block, and the SAME id appears in the Media List row URL the comment is anchored to, so the ids correspond between body and Media List. Conservative: only a shared reference NUMBER matches (no fuzzy/title match); cross-form (body gm vs media-list /id/) is rare since forms are consistent within a module. Set id_match:false to match on the exact URL only; MEDIAMATCH_OFF still disables the whole feature.

match.note: Word stores w:author as the person's Office display name, which VARIES: space-form ('Nadia Stanton') vs dot/username-form ('Kate.Scanlon'), and case ('caroline schwer', 'simon vita', 'amanda griffiths'). Matching normalises both author and whitelist: lowercase, collapse whitespace, treat '.' as a space, strip a trailing ' [N]' Word disambiguator, and also accept 'Last First' order. Across all the corpus authors, the six below have NO unmatched variant, and no OTHER author normalises into one of them.
